title: the lac house
hook: as the Pandavas leave, Vidura warns Yudhishthira in words nobody else can follow, and in Varanavata the new house smells wrong

segments.voice: Yesterday, the lac house was planned: a holiday offered, a blind king persuaded, a house built to burn. Did any offer make you ask what it was made of? Day seven hundred thirty-five.

A farewell at the edge of the city. The Pandavas and their mother are setting out for Varanavata, and a crowd has followed them out, unhappy to see them go. Vidura, their uncle, walks beside Yudhishthira. Then he says something strange. The words are in a tongue the crowd doesn't understand, the text says, a language that only Yudhishthira can follow. To anyone listening, it sounds like a riddle. To Yudhishthira, it's a warning. Today in the lac house, a message is passed in plain sight.
screen: `A FAREWELL AT THE CITY'S EDGE.` → `VIDURA SPEAKS IN A HIDDEN TONGUE.` → `A WARNING IN PLAIN SIGHT.`

segments.voice: Vidura's riddle goes something like this. There's a weapon not made of steel that can still destroy a body; whoever knows it can't be killed by it. A fire that burns a whole forest can't reach the creatures that live in holes underground. Someone who knows the roads, who can find the way by the stars, will survive. Fire, holes, roads, stars. Yudhishthira answers simply: I have understood. Later, on the road, Kunti asks him what all that was about, and he tells her: Vidura was warning us of fire. Then they arrive. Varanavata welcomes them with joy. Purochana greets them warmly, and after some days moves them into the new house. And Yudhishthira, walking through it, catches a smell: fat, and lac. He turns to Bhima. This house, he says, is made to burn. Now step back and look at this week. Karna gave away his armor. Karna walked into an arena and only his mother knew him. Karna was crowned and mocked in a single afternoon. And then a plot was laid, and a warning given in words no one else could read. It's a week of hidden things: a hidden brother, a hidden grief, a hidden trap, a hidden message. The Mahabharata keeps putting the listener in on secrets the characters don't share. Today, at least, one of the hidden things is caught in time.
screen: `FIRE, HOLES, ROADS, STARS.` · `I HAVE UNDERSTOOD.` · `THE HOUSE SMELLS OF LAC.` · `A WEEK OF HIDDEN THINGS.` · then, large: `THIS HOUSE IS MADE TO BURN.`

segments.voice: A week ends today, so take two slow minutes. Let the breath settle. Recall a warning someone gave you once, gently, maybe sideways, that you only understood later. Or one you were given this week. Who gave it? If thanks rises for them, even if you didn't listen, let it. Then just rest and notice the room you're in, its sounds, its smells, the way Yudhishthira noticed his. The bell holds the time.
The lac house. Vidura's riddle of fire, holes, roads and stars, Yudhishthira's answer, I have understood, and a house that smells of lac.
Your line: the lac house. Today, listen for the warning inside an ordinary sentence, and thank whoever says it. Day seven hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Vidura is honored in Hindu tradition as a figure of wisdom and good counsel, and his coded warning at Varanavata is one of the scenes told to show it.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. your uncle has just warned you in riddles of fire and holes in the ground. the crowd is watching. what do you do?
options: ask him to say it plainly.
fork.reveal: he answers: I have understood. he explains it to Kunti later, on the road, and goes on to Varanavata.

original.note: Sanskrit vidura: the name of the Pandavas' wise uncle who sends the warning.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas walk into the trap without a clue.
what it means: Vidura warns Yudhishthira in a hidden tongue, and he recognizes the house by its smell.
what a scholar hears: the riddle's images, a weapon not of steel, a fire that can't reach creatures in holes, point ahead to how the brothers will survive.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Jatugriha Parva (Vidura's warning in a hidden tongue; Yudhishthira's reply; arrival at Varanavata; Yudhishthira recognizes the house)

notes: All paraphrase. Ganguli calls Vidura's language the Mlechchha tongue; the script says only 'a tongue only Yudhishthira can follow' to avoid an unexplained term. A Keeper may prefer to name it.

Vidura's riddle is condensed (weapon not of steel, fire that can't reach creatures in holes, finding the way by the stars); 'I have understood' is a paraphrase of Yudhishthira's reply, not a quotation. Confirm the gist.
